rowText: The cause of the one-second wait: read what is in memory before, during and after an ask. The Deck has been wiped and set up again since 2026-09-12, so a fresh reading was worth taking.

setup.question: what game am i playing
setup.how_read: ollama ps over SSH, read three times around one ask

readings.result: gemma4:e2b-it-qat, 1.7 GB, 100% GPU, kept for 4 hours

readings.when: during the ask, while it was still streaming (~09:40:00)
readings.result: nothing listed -- the model was not in memory at that moment
gemma4:e2b-it-qat, 1.7 GB, 100% GPU, kept for 4 hours -- back in memory

plugin_log_lines: [2026-09-18 09:40:39,136][INFO]: ask_ollama: stream done model=gemma4:e2b-it-qat done_reason=stop eval_count=604 prompt_eval=1530 raw_len=687 visible_len=410 num_predict=2112 think=True
verdictSentence: Caught it happening: partway through answering, the one chat model this Deck uses actually disappeared from memory for a moment, then came back once the answer was done. That is the wait a person notices -- the model gets swapped out and back in during a single question, on this Deck as set up today.
notes: Only one chat model is configured on this Deck (gemma4:e2b-it-qat, per settings.json's text/vision routing), so the eviction is not a hand-off to a second named model -- something else (most likely the note-search/embedding step) is briefly taking the GPU slot mid-answer and the chat model is reloaded afterward. Which exact settings this Deck runs for the hold-one-model-at-a-time behaviour was not changed, only read.
